summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent pipes remote WebSocket bytes into a spawned PTY, giving the WS peer full-host RCE
details: When the operator starts the agent (via the `yeaft-agent`/`yeaft` bin or the installed systemd/launchd/PM2 service), it opens an outbound WebSocket to `ctx.CONFIG.serverUrl` and routes server-sent messages to handlers that spawn a bash/PowerShell PTY (`pty.spawn(shell,...)` in `terminal.js` handleTerminalCreate) and then write attacker-supplied bytes into that PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)` on `terminal_input`). Additional message types perform arbitrary filesystem and git operations (`write_file`, `delete_files`, `git_push`,...) driven by the same remote peer. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket server therefore has interactive shell and file-write access on the operator's host. A separate `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to run `npm install -g @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restart, allowing the same remote peer to force re-pull and execution of any future published version. Trigger timing is at agent startup, not `npm install` or `require()`; the harm materializes once the operator runs the tool against a hostile or compromised server.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
